request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person can now have an approver, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**How it works**
- **Stored data:** a new migration `V100__person_approver.sql` adds a nullable `approver` column to `person`. A cloned sheet copies the approver along with the rest of the person.
- **Setting it:** `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/people/{id}/approver` with body `{ user }`. The name is trimmed and a blank one is refused. A successful set writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=… by=… name=<person> user=<user>` to the audit file.
- **Approving and rejecting:** the server check behind approve and reject (`ClaimService.pending`) now lets through a steward or the person's approver. The existing rules still apply on top of that, so whoever opened the claim or last edited it still can't approve it.
- **Screen:** each person row now shows the approver (`person-approver`), with an entry (`person-approver-input`) and a "Set approver" button (`person-approver-save`). A refusal shows on the row's existing `person-error`.

**Decisions you may want to change**
- Any user who can edit the sheet can set an approver. Viewers are still blocked by the existing viewer guard. The spec has a clerk set it, so I didn't limit it to stewards.
- There is no way to remove an approver once set, because blank names are refused. The request didn't ask for one.

**A fix outside the request:** scenario 3 failed on `rollup-cut-total` because of a bug that was already there. The table that holds imported opening balances (`PERIOD_PERSON_OPENING`) was missing from the list of tables `SheetPasts` saves and restores when showing the sheet as of a past date. After an opening was imported, the pools list failed with a 409, so every cut showed 0.00. I added the table to `SheetPasts.TABLES`.
